note: 'I will go with you, answered Abishai. That night David and Abishai came to the troops' (1Sam 26:6-7). He offers to kill Saul and David forbids it.
One of the two David puts the question to at the edge of Saul's camp (1Sam 26:6).

'And said to Saul, Why do you listen to the words of men who say, Look, David intends to harm you?' (1Sam 24:9), holding up the cut skirt as proof, and closing 'May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me' (24:15).
'So David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing.' (2Sam 6:12), dancing before it girded in a linen ephod (6:14).
Sworn at 18:3 and again at 20:42, and honoured at 2Sam 9:1 -- 'to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan'.
'So David gave his oath to Saul' (1Sam 24:22).
'So David said to Abner, You are a man, aren’t you? ... Why then did you not protect your lord the king?' (1Sam 26:15), with the king's own spear in his hand as the evidence.

'Thus the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household.' (2Sam 6:11). The blessing is what persuades David to resume a journey he had abandoned in fear.
'So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David' (1Sam 20:16), binding David's descendants to spare his own.

'should it please my father to do you evil, if I don’t disclose it to you and send you away, that you may go in peace' (1Sam 20:13), carried out with three arrows and a lad who is told nothing (20:35-39).

'How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” she said. “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects' (2Sam 6:20), having watched from a window and despised him in her heart (6:16). The chapter closes without reconciling them: 'And Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death' (6:23).

'Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him. So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.' (1Sam 20:33). The throw aimed at the son settles the question about the son-in-law.
Saul asks for the oath and David swears it (1Sam 24:21-22).
'Then Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, You son of a perverse and rebellious woman' (1Sam 20:30) -- for having chosen David over his own succession.
'Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi. So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David' (1Sam 24:1-2).
'So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David' (1Sam 26:2) -- the same number of men as at En-gedi two chapters before.
'And there was a steward of the house of Saul named Ziba.' (2Sam 9:2); 'Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba' (9:9).
Twice, in the same words and to the same effect (1Sam 23:19, 26:1).
